translation.goal: Constrain the first `drivers/net/dummy_rust.rs` to the minimal registration, setup, validate, and lifecycle loops required by the upstream dummy net driver while keeping the net-link-type abstraction surface intact.
translation.abstraction_goal: Keep the Rust artifact inside the existing `net::rtnl` + `net::netdevice` + `net::stats` stack so the tool can reason about link-type registration, netdev ops wiring, and the trivial xmit/stat paths without inventing new unsafe helpers.

mvp_scope.target_command: ip link add dummy0 type dummy && ip link set dummy0 up && ip link set dummy0 down && ip link del dummy0
mvp_scope.note: Phase-1 Rust driver should cover lifecycle registration plus wired netdev ops that keep packets dropped but stats updated.

body_plan: Run the typed equivalent of `ether_setup`, then wire the module-specific `netdev_ops`/`ethtool_ops` and device flags (no-ARP, no multicast, random MAC, xmit-limited features).
Keep netdev field writes inside the wrapper rather than touching `bindings::*` directly.
Translate `tb[IFLA_ADDRESS]` checks into `ValidateContext` helpers that enforce length `ETH_ALEN` and address validity.
Return typed `Err(EINVAL)`/`Err(EADDRNOTAVAIL)` when the upstream checks fail.
Set `pcpu_stat_type` through the typed setter and keep the `netdev_lockdep_set_classes` call inside the helper/module shim.
Record the packet length with `stats::dev_lstats_add`, timestamp via `skb::timestamp`, and drop it through the safe `SkBuff` ownership helpers while returning `TxOutcome::Ok`.
Delegate to the existing `eth_validate_addr` abstraction exposed by `netdevice::eth`.
Mirror the upstream empty implementation so the Rust shim can stay in place while keeping the MAC/multicast flags managed elsewhere.
Route to the existing `eth_mac_addr` helper so the module does not claim new bindgen constants.
Expose the per-CPU stats read via the typed wrapper that mirrors `dev_lstats_read`.
Call `netif::carrier_on` or `netif::carrier_off` through the wrapper based on the requested carrier state.

netdev_ops.note: The wrapper should publish the ld-inside `net_device_ops` struct so the setup path can borrow the static reference.

ethtool_ops.note: Expose the minimal ethtool ops handler that only routes `get_ts_info`.

needs_free_netdev.note: Keep the ownership policy identical to the upstream driver.

request_ops_lock.note: Mirror the C field to keep the lock owner consistent.

flags.note: Enforce the no-ARP/multicast bits inside typed setters.

priv_flags.note: Preserve the same private-flag combination the C driver writes.

lltx.note: Keep the lockless transmit marker in the wrapper.

features.rust_surface: dev.add_features(netdevice::features::SG | netdevice::features::FRAGLIST | netdevice::features::GSO_SOFTWARE | netdevice::features::HW_CSUM | netdevice::features::HIGHDMA | netdevice::features::GSO_ENCAP_ALL)
features.note: Mirror the chained `|=` calls through a single typed call.

hw_features.note: Copy the feature set into the hardware feature mask after the driver features are known.

hw_enc_features.note: Equalize encoded hardware features to stay in sync with the C driver.

min_mtu.note: Keep the low MTU bound that the C setup assigns.

max_mtu.note: Keep the upper MTU bound that the C setup assigns.

validate_translation_rules.note: Use typed attr helpers instead of raw `nla_len`.
Route the address check through the existing `eth` helper.

private_state.note: Dummy driver keeps no per-device private storage.
